app.tagline: An innovative student platform that turns dialogue into a starting point for growth — blending individual and group sessions with intelligent tools to understand needs, discover strengths, and empower students to shape their paths with confidence.

about.title: About the Companion
about.lede: A quiet decision-support tool built for school counselors working with adolescent students.
about.purposeBody: To help counselors better attune to their students during sessions by surfacing real-time biometric signals — heart rate, skin response, motion — alongside the conversation. Suggested approaches from an AI model help the counselor decide when to slow down, reflect back, or shift topic.
about.howBody: A student wears a small wristband with medical-grade sensors. The counselor's browser pairs with the device via Bluetooth. Every few seconds a bundle of readings and a transcript segment goes to a private server, and an AI returns a brief state summary and 1–3 suggested conversational moves — visible only on the counselor's screen.
about.boundariesBody: This is not a diagnostic tool. It never labels a student with a condition, never suggests medication or clinical referral without human review, and never displays anything to the student. It's decision-support for a trained counselor — nothing more.
about.framingNote: 🌱 روافد — we listen, we understand, we empower.

overview.title: How it works
overview.lede: Eight steps, from onboarding a student to reviewing a session afterward.

step1.title: Add the student to your roster
step1.body: The counselor enters basic information — name, grade, school ID — from the Students page.

step2.title: Record parental + student consent
step2.body: No session can begin until a Guardian's signed consent is on file. This is enforced by the platform, not just a policy.

step3.title: Pair the wearable device
step3.body: At the start of a session, the counselor's Chrome/Edge browser pairs with the ESP32 wristband over Web Bluetooth. A Simulate button lets you exercise the flow without hardware.

step4.title: Live signal ingestion
step4.body: Every ~3–5 seconds the wearable pushes a bundle of readings (HR, HRV, GSR, skin temp, motion) to the platform, which stores them and updates a live chart on the counselor's screen.

step5.title: Rolling AI guidance
step5.body: Every ~15 seconds Claude analyzes the window and returns a plain-language state summary plus 1–3 suggested conversational moves. The counselor sees this on a private card during the session.

step6.title: Session replay + reports
step6.body: After the session, the counselor can browse charts, the AI timeline, and the transcript. Per-student and per-session PDF reports are printable.

step7.title: Audit log
step7.body: Every read of a student's session, biometric, or consent record is logged with actor + timestamp. Foundation admins review the audit trail.

step8.title: Foundation oversight
step8.body: Across-school aggregates for the Foundation. Individual student biometric detail is deliberately not visible from that view — the counselor is the trusted human in the loop.

support.lede: We're here to help — reach out by email or open the FAQ below.
support.emailBody: General questions about setup, permissions, or how a feature works.
support.escalateBody: Time-sensitive issues around student data, consent, or session errors — reach the platform lead directly.

faq1.q: What data does the platform store about a student?
faq1.a: Basic profile (name, ID, grade), consent record with guardian info, and per-session biometric samples + transcript + AI analyses. No raw audio is stored by default. Access is limited to the counselor of the student's school.

faq2.q: Can the AI ever be shown to the student?
faq2.a: No. The AI's state summary and suggested approaches are visible only on the counselor's private dashboard. The platform has no UI that ever surfaces AI output to the student.

faq3.q: What if a parent asks for their child's data to be deleted?
faq3.a: The counselor can revoke consent from the student profile, which soft-deletes future access. For full erasure, contact the platform lead — a manual purge is honored per the Foundation's data-handling policy.

faq4.q: Which browsers work with the wearable?
faq4.a: Web Bluetooth pairing requires Chrome or Edge on desktop, or Chrome on Android. Safari and iOS do not support Web Bluetooth — use the Simulate mode for testing on those platforms.
